title: Ob spring volume and pulse width had a positive relation in 1936-1975, with a near-zero lower block limit
abstract: We tested a published Ob River spring volume-width lead in 40 complete certified years from 1936 to 1975. These years do not overlap the earlier study sample of 1980-2011. After linear year trends were removed, the correlation between log April-July flow volume and central 60% flow width was 0.362. Conditional 95% five-year block limits were 0.004 to 0.683. An added 100,000-draw check gave 0.008 to 0.680. The result gives modest support for a positive relation in the earlier period. Three- and seven-year block checks also gave positive lower limits. A circular phase reference gave 1/40. The later-period estimate was 0.359. The early-minus-late difference was 0.003, with limits of -0.441 to 0.417, so the test does not establish equal relations or a change. Adding August gave 0.481, and adding a local flow midpoint control gave 0.697. Regulation, shared flow errors, fixed windows, short records and conditional uncertainty limit interpretation. This is a test in separate years from the same source product, not independent instrument confirmation. Code, aggregate evidence, a figure, source hashes and an independent arithmetic audit support reproduction. Daily and annual source records remain external.

display.caption: Ob volume-width estimates and conditional 95% block limits. Early means 1936-1975; later means 1980-2011. Checks use different flow or dependence definitions. The primary lower limit is close to zero.

citations.reason: Tests its positive Ob lead with new code in non-overlapping earlier years. Source product and gauge are the same. Support is conditional and modest.
Its width and dependence results inform caution about fixed windows and near-zero block limits.
